---
title: "Men vs Women"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/data-prep.R")

beach_athlete_age_records <- beach_athletes |>
  filter(!is.na(age)) |>
  mutate(
    medal_status = case_when(
      is.na(medal) & year >= 2020 ~ "Not reported in source",
      is.na(medal) ~ "No medal",
      TRUE ~ as.character(medal)
    ),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", name, "</b>",
      "<br>Country: ", country, " (NOC: ", noc, ")",
      "<br>Olympic year: ", year,
      "<br>Event: ", gender, " beach volleyball",
      "<br>Age: ", age, " years",
      "<br>Medal status: ", medal_status
    )
  )

athlete_profiles <- beach_athlete_age_records |>
  filter(!is.na(height)) |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", name, "</b>",
      "<br>Country: ", country, " (NOC: ", noc, ")",
      "<br>Olympic year: ", year,
      "<br>Event: ", gender, " beach volleyball",
      "<br>Age: ", age, " years",
      "<br>Height: ", height, " cm",
      "<br>Medal status: ", medal_status
    )
  )

men_age_median <- median(
  beach_athlete_age_records$age[beach_athlete_age_records$gender == "Men"]
)
women_age_median <- median(
  beach_athlete_age_records$age[beach_athlete_age_records$gender == "Women"]
)
men_height_count <- sum(athlete_profiles$gender == "Men")
women_height_count <- sum(athlete_profiles$gender == "Women")
men_missing_height_count <- sum(
  is.na(beach_athletes$height) & beach_athletes$gender == "Men"
)
women_missing_height_count <- sum(
  is.na(beach_athletes$height) & beach_athletes$gender == "Women"
)
men_team_medals <- sum(beach_medals$gender == "Men")
women_team_medals <- sum(beach_medals$gender == "Women")
```

## Participation matched after 2000; age and podiums show smaller differences

Since 2000, the men's and women's events each have 48 athlete-event records at every Games; in 1996, the women's event had 36 compared with 48 for men. Across all editions, the median recorded age is **`r men_age_median`** for men and **`r women_age_median`** for women. Each event has earned 24 team medals.

An athlete-event record is one person's participation in one Games and event, not a unique athlete. The **`r nrow(beach_athlete_age_records)`** age records represent **`r dplyr::n_distinct(beach_athlete_age_records$id)`** distinct source IDs; returning athletes appear in more than one record.

### Age distributions across the two events

The distributions overlap substantially. The median age is **`r men_age_median`** in the men's event and **`r women_age_median`** in the women's event; each dot is one real source record.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "One point per beach-volleyball athlete-event record with reported age. Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes."

age_distribution_chart <- ggplot(
  beach_athlete_age_records,
  aes(
    x = gender,
    y = age,
    color = gender,
    text = hover_text
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.22, height = 0, seed = 2024),
    alpha = 0.35,
    size = 1.9
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Men = "#147f91", Women = "#c99837")) +
  labs(
    title = "Age distributions overlap across the men's and women's events",
    x = "Event",
    y = "Age (years)",
    color = "Event"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#355260"),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#10384a", face = "bold")
  )

plotly::ggplotly(age_distribution_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
**Observation count:** **`r nrow(beach_athlete_age_records)`** age-reported athlete-event records and the same number of plotted points; **`r dplyr::n_distinct(beach_athlete_age_records$id)`** distinct source IDs. All beach-volleyball records in this source have an age.
:::

### Individual athlete profiles

This height-versus-age view retains the existing individual profiles. Points are colored by event and shaped by medal status where the source reports it.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes. Shows ", scales::comma(nrow(athlete_profiles)), " of ", scales::comma(nrow(beach_athletes)), " athlete-event records with reported height; medal status is unavailable in the source for 2020 and 2024.")'

profile_chart <- ggplot(
  athlete_profiles,
  aes(
    x = age,
    y = height,
    color = gender,
    shape = medal_status,
    text = hover_text
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, alpha = 0.72) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Men = "#147f91", Women = "#c99837")) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "Gold" = 17,
      "Silver" = 15,
      "Bronze" = 18,
      "No medal" = 16,
      "Not reported in source" = 4
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Height (cm)",
    color = "Event",
    shape = "Medal status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#355260")
  )

plotly::ggplotly(profile_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
**Observation count:** **`r nrow(athlete_profiles)`** of **`r nrow(beach_athletes)`** athlete-event records have reported age and height and are plotted; **`r nrow(beach_athletes) - nrow(athlete_profiles)`** lack height. Medal status is not reported by this source for 2020 or 2024.
:::

### Height distributions

Height is reported for **`r nrow(athlete_profiles)`** of **`r nrow(beach_athletes)`** athlete-event records. That is enough for a descriptive comparison, but missing heights are noted rather than assumed to match the observed records.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "One point per beach-volleyball athlete-event record with reported height. Heights are in centimeters; source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes."

height_distribution_chart <- ggplot(
  athlete_profiles,
  aes(
    x = gender,
    y = height,
    color = gender,
    text = hover_text
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.18, height = 0, seed = 2024),
    alpha = 0.4,
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Men = "#147f91", Women = "#c99837")) +
  labs(
    title = "Recorded heights differ between the events",
    x = "Event",
    y = "Height (cm)",
    color = "Event"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#355260"),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#10384a", face = "bold")
  )

plotly::ggplotly(height_distribution_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
**Observation count:** **`r nrow(athlete_profiles)`** reported heights are plotted: **`r men_height_count`** men's and **`r women_height_count`** women's records. Height is missing for **`r nrow(beach_athletes) - nrow(athlete_profiles)`** records (**`r men_missing_height_count`** men and **`r women_missing_height_count`** women). Median recorded height is **`r median(athlete_profiles$height[athlete_profiles$gender == "Men"])` cm** for men and **`r median(athlete_profiles$height[athlete_profiles$gender == "Women"])` cm** for women.
:::

### Participation through the years

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Athlete-event participation by event and Olympic year. Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes."

participation_chart <- ggplot(
  beach_participation_by_year,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = athlete_event_records,
    color = gender,
    group = gender,
    text = paste0(
      gender,
      " event<br>Olympic year: ", year,
      "<br>Athlete-event records: ", athlete_event_records
    )
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Men = "#147f91", Women = "#c99837")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(beach_participation_by_year$year))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    title = "Participation entries match at every Games since 2000",
    x = "Olympic year",
    y = "Athlete-event records",
    color = "Event",
    caption = "Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes; beach volleyball identified from the event field."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#637780", hjust = 0)
  )

plotly::ggplotly(participation_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
**Observation count:** **`r nrow(beach_athletes)`** athlete-event records are aggregated to **`r nrow(beach_participation_by_year)`** year-by-event points (eight editions and two events). These counts measure listed participation, not audience or popularity.
:::

### Who reached the podium?

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Each point is one of 48 medal-winning country-teams. Panels compare men's and women's results by Olympic year; 2020 and 2024 podiums use official Olympic results."

gender_medal_chart <- beach_medals |>
  mutate(
    country = factor(country, levels = rev(country_medal_totals$country)),
    year = factor(year, levels = sort(unique(year)))
  ) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = country,
      color = medal,
      text = paste(country, gender, year, medal, "team medal")
    )
  ) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.65),
    size = 2.8
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~gender, ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(Gold = "#c99837", Silver = "#9caab5", Bronze = "#b87950"),
    breaks = c("Gold", "Silver", "Bronze")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Olympic year",
    y = "Medal-winning country",
    color = "Medal",
    caption = "Medals count country-teams, not athletes. 2020 and 2024 podiums use official Olympic results."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#10384a"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#637780", hjust = 0)
  )

plotly::ggplotly(gender_medal_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
Sources: `olympicAthletes` for 1996–2016; official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. The plot shows all **`r scales::comma(nrow(beach_medals))`** country-team medal results once each, not once per athlete.
:::

**Observation count:** **`r nrow(beach_medals)`** medal-winning country-teams produce **`r nrow(beach_medals)`** points, **`r men_team_medals`** per event. Brazil leads both tallies (8 women's and 6 men's medals), while the United States has 7 women's and 4 men's; Australia's three medals are all in the women's event. These are team results, not individual athlete medals.
